source.title: A reexamination of the evidence for the somatic marker hypothesis: what participants really know in the Iowa gambling task.
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: High confidence that this paper removes one of the three biological groundings INV-040's notes cite by name, and does so on the strongest methodological footing available -- a direct re-run with more sensitive knowledge probes, showing participants report the advantageous strategy MORE reliably than they behave advantageously. Lower confidence that it bears on INV-040's actual content, because what it falsifies is the NONCONSCIOUS half of Bechara's interpretation, and INV-040 asserts cue-sufficiency and temporal precedence, not nonconsciousness. Registered as weakens rather than mixed because the honest effect on this claim is real: its cited evidential base is thinner than the notes imply.
failure_signatures: When more sensitive probes are used, participants' reportable knowledge is sufficient to guide advantageous choice, so no cue-driven pre-declarative biasing signal needs to be posited to explain the behaviour -- the phenomenon INV-040 borrows as grounding may be an artefact of insensitive measurement rather than a mechanism.

A REE analogue of this failure: if w_harm elevation on cue-present steps is measured with an instrument coarse enough to miss that z_harm_a has already begun to move, an apparent 'cue precedes accumulation' result can be produced by measurement lag alone. Any INV-040 experiment must therefore condition explicitly on z_harm_a being below its accumulation threshold, not merely early in the episode.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Using more sensitive knowledge-assessment methods, participants in the Iowa Gambling Task demonstrate substantially more reportable knowledge of the advantageous strategy than Bechara et al. reported -- in fact reporting it more reliably than they act on it -- so both choice and report can be explained by sampling from consciously accessible knowledge without appeal to nonconscious somatic markers.
mapping.ree_translation: One of the three sources INV-040's notes cite as biological grounding (Bechara et al. 1997) does not carry the weight the notes place on it. For REE the transferable lesson is methodological rather than mechanistic: an apparent 'cue acts before the accumulator' result is only as good as the sensitivity of the instrument measuring the accumulator, and a coarse accumulator readout manufactures spurious precedence.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This paper attacks the consciousness claim, not the timing claim. It does not show that cue-driven anticipatory states are absent, and it does not test whether a partial sensory cue can configure a defensive terrain -- it shows that this particular task does not require nonconscious mediation to explain the behaviour. Treating it as a refutation of INV-040 itself would overreach; treating it as leaving INV-040's cited grounding weaker than advertised is the defensible reading, and is what is recorded here.
mapping.source_context: Human adults, Iowa Gambling Task, re-run with denser and more granular knowledge probes than the original self-report schedule; behavioural and verbal-report measures, no lesion group.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high -- PNAS, direct methodological replication of the exact paradigm, widely cited and broadly accepted as having shifted the field's reading of the original. Mapping fidelity deliberately mid-range: the target of the disconfirmation is adjacent to, not identical with, what INV-040 asserts, and saying so plainly is more useful to governance than inflating it into a clean falsifier.
